races.name: Irish EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Paphos
runners_data.note: Completely unknown quantity with no form data and lightly-raced flag; Declan Carroll's stable is running cold at 0/12 over 14 days, which reduces confidence in a debut-type winner here, and the U style designation means tactical placement is guesswork.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Star
runners_data.note: Finished 11th on debut over 6f on good ground but drops to a sharper 5f today which may suit better; Billy Garritty takes the ride for a yard that has found form at 3/37 in the 14-day window, though the fade-in-finish flag is a real concern in a race that will be run at a strong pace.

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: Two solid placed efforts from the front over 5-6f on good ground make this the most consistently reliable front-runner in the field; Jason Hart is a shrewd operator from the lead and the horse's 21-day freshener is untroubling, though it will need to see off Sable Noir's challenge early or risk being drawn into a war it cannot win.

runners_data.name: By Jove Grace
runners_data.note: Fahey's runner has placed form at 5f on good ground and is a natural hold-up horse that the pace map has had to shift forward to midfield because the rear of the field is already at capacity — its true racing style means it would prefer to sit last and finish through, and being forced to race out of role tempers its winning prospects in this shape.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: The most experienced horse in the field with six runs showing consistent placed form at 5f on good ground; David O'Meara and Daniel Tudhope is a powerful combination, and the horse's pattern of finishing third and fourth suggests it finds a level and keeps it — it fits the stalker profile perfectly for Scenario A.

runners_data.name: Classyfied
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's runner finished fifth on good ground over 5f on debut and holds an H style tag; Sean Kirrane partners it at 3/90 for the yard in the 14-day window, which is a cold stat, but the hold-up profile means it could benefit quietly if the front end blows up.

runners_data.name: La Flor Granada
runners_data.note: A Fahey second string who finished eighth over 6f on soft ground last time out and carries a fade flag alongside lightly-raced status; dropping to 5f on a sounder surface could sharpen things up, but there is little evidence here to build a strong case, and the trainer's second runner in the same race is a complicating factor.

runners_data.name: Sable Noir
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's runner was beaten into eighth on debut at 5f on good ground and carries both a fade flag and hood headgear; the yard is quiet at 1/36 over 14 days and 63 days off the track is a notable gap — the front-running profile is confirmed but the fade flag means it may cut out the pace and stop if headed by The Mean Fiddler.

races.paceDynamic: Sable Noir and The Mean Fiddler are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates on this straight 5f at Musselburgh, creating a genuinely contested early pace rather than a solo dawdle. The Mean Fiddler has shown consistent placed form pressing on from the front over course-relevant distances on good ground, while Sable Noir carries a fade flag, suggesting the early duel may hollow out both leaders in the final furlong. With two genuine pace angles fighting for the same position, the gallop will be honest and the race is likely to be set up for horses sitting just off the speed — Calef and By Jove Grace's natural closer profile becomes the theoretical beneficiary, though By Jove Grace is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because genuine rear-gang types are already at capacity in this shape. This field carries more front-running and prominent energy than the track can absorb cleanly, with Sable Noir and The Mean Fiddler most likely to actually secure the early positions; the contested pace tilts this race shape firmly in favour of prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can travel sweetly and pounce through the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Sable Noir and The Mean Fiddler burn each other off and a prominent-sitting horse travels within striking distance to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a genuine clip that drains their reserves, leaving the race wide open for a horse sitting second or third and travelling kindly into the final furlong. Calef's consistent placed form on good ground over 5f and Pivotal Star's hold-up profile converting to an early delivery both fit this shape well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler gets a clean break and finds a rhythm without being harried hard by Sable Noir, controlling the tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: The Mean Fiddler has two placed runs from the front on good ground at comparable distances and knows how to establish a comfortable lead; if Sable Noir fades early after the initial duel, The Mean Fiddler could find itself in a rhythm that the field cannot disrupt. The prominent horses would be unable to close the gap on a 5f flat track when a front-runner finds their stride unchallenged after the first furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Fliers Land
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is scorching and the whole field is stretched, creating genuine late ground for hold-up horses to finish through.
scenarios.body: A furiously-run duel leaves the front end spent, and a horse with enough sprint reserve can pick off tired rivals in the final 100 yards. By Jove Grace is the natural beneficiary here as a true hold-up type, though its redistribution to midfield means it is unlikely to be at the rear of the field where this scenario best plays out, tempering the probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Scenario Scrambles
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners clash for position causing interference or one checks sharply, shuffling the order and handing a benefit to a horse with a wide draw who avoids the trouble.
scenarios.body: A chaotic early phase rewards whoever avoids the melee and picks up a clean run through, potentially gifting an unlikely winner from an unexposed or lightly-raced profile. Paphos as an unknown quantity and La Flor Granada, while fading from far back last time, could benefit if the principals cancel each other out violently and the race becomes a sprint from halfway.

watchPoints.text: Sable Noir's fade flag combined with its front-running style creates a live danger that it sets a strong gallop and then stops abruptly in the final furlong, causing interference for horses attempting to pass on its inside.

The Mean Fiddler and Sable Noir occupying the same tactical space risks a bumping or crowding incident in the opening furlong — watch for either horse being forced off its stride before the race settles.

By Jove Grace is a genuine hold-up type racing out of role in midfield; if it gets squeezed for room in a congested middle section, its chance could be compromised before it reaches the furlong marker.

Calef has an unresolved query on its most recent 5f run in the form data — connections will know if there was an excuse, and any market move for Tudhope's mount in the ring should be noted given the horse's otherwise consistent placed profile on this ground.

La Flor Granada and By Jove Grace run for the same trainer in the same race — watch which of the two attracts stronger market support closer to post time as that will indicate where Fahey's stable confidence sits.

races.name: National Racehorse Week Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Forest Berry
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's operation fires at 5/21 over 14 days and this filly has placed twice on similar going including a win at the trip; fitted with hood (hg:h), she is a natural prominent racer who should sit just off Le Grand Etoile and is perfectly positioned for the dominant race shape.
runners_data.comment: Forest Berry wins last time out and had a second three starts back to underline her claims, and with experience over today's trip and a solid rating edge over her rivals, she is the one to beat off 141 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Rule Of The Agency
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard has been quiet (3/90 over 14 days) but Jason Hart partners a horse whose three runs have all come over this distance on Good ground with a placed effort; naturally a hold-up type, she will need things to develop in the straight rather than winning from a position she can fully control.
runners_data.comment: Rule Of The Agency was third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 69 ranking him second among the seven runners — though he is yet to score in recent starts and a trainer strike-rate of just 3% over the past fortnight is the clear concern.

runners_data.name: Bonjour Belle
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's runner has placed form on similar going and stays the trip, but her true racing style is as a hold-up horse — in a race with too many closers for the map to accommodate, she is likely to find herself in midfield rather than off the back, which dulls the late-run threat she needs to produce.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Bonjour Belle at least showed some encouragement with a fourth two runs back, and she has experience over today's trip and going; carrying 122 lb from stall two, she rates a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Etoile
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner is the only confirmed front-runner in the field and Andrew Mullen can set his own terms with zero pressure; form figures are uninspiring (best is a fifth from four runs) and 41 days off the track is a minor flag, but his tactical role is clear and he controls the race's early shape entirely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, Le Grand Etoile faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 41 days carrying 119 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Astral Calling
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's yard is in form (8/43 over 14 days) and Jack Nicholls claims 3lb on a horse whose three starts have all been over this distance on Good or Good-equivalent ground; a genuine come-from-behind type by nature, the crowded hold-up zone means he will race further forward than ideal, limiting his typical finishing kick.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Astral Calling faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and returns on a quick 12-day turnaround suggesting she is fit enough to show more.

runners_data.name: Bluestone Lady
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan partners a filly with a win on Good ground over 7f and the best sim-going record in the field (6/9 with 1W1P); blinkers fitted (hg:b) and 17 days since her last run, she is a natural hold-up type who will need to be produced late, but her class edge at OR 64 gives her scope to overcome a less-than-perfect pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Bluestone Lady won two starts back and was a solid fourth last time out, returning after just 17 days in good order; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, and at 134 lb the weight burden is the one factor to weigh up.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Rocket
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's runner has three runs all on Good or similar going but no wins or places to show for them; a true come-from-behind type whose style fit is compromised in this race because the rear of the field is congested, and Billy Garritty will find less room to manoeuvre than a genuine hold-up specialist requires.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, The Resdev Rocket nevertheless appeals as a leading threat here, having run over today's trip and going before and arriving on a quick 17-day turnaround in good heart; the main concern is that his recent finishes of fifth, seventh and eighth suggest a return to form is still needed.

races.paceDynamic: Le Grand Etoile is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Andrew Mullen can dictate his own unhurried gallop from the front around Musselburgh's tight flat circuit. A sustainable, uncontested pace over one mile on Good ground typically sets up a race that rewards horses who can track close to the leader and produce a sustained finish from a handy position, rather than those waiting for a sprint that may never fully materialise. Forest Berry and Rule Of The Agency, as the primary prominent and hold-up representatives with genuine claims, are best placed to exploit that shape. This field carries significantly more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Bonjour Belle, Astral Calling, and The Resdev Rocket are natural come-from-behind types who will find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than off the true back of the field, meaning the late rush they need may not develop with a modest, unchallenged pace in front. The race shape strongly favours a prominent or close-tracking profile: horses who settle just behind the leader and strike when Le Grand Etoile is headed in the closing stages hold the clearest positional advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Le Grand Etoile dictates a controlled, uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking close throughout.
scenarios.body: Andrew Mullen sets an honest but unhurried pace and a prominent challenger strikes before the hold-up brigade can organise their runs; the flat track and Good ground mean there is no premium on a late burst when the pace is managed. Horses with a close-tracking profile who have the fitness and the jockey craft to be positioned second or third at the turn for home benefit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If Le Grand Etoile's pace is genuinely sustainable at this trip and no prominent rival applies enough pressure to dislodge him in the straight.
scenarios.body: With seven runners and no challenger willing to push the pace, Le Grand Etoile could steal enough of a margin through the final furlong to hold every challenge; his form figures are modest but uncontested front-runners at this level have won on less. This outcome depends on his rivals underestimating his stamina for a mile at this sedate tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply through the middle of the race and creates a true end-to-end gallop that strings the field out and leaves a gap for closers.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given only one genuine pace-setter, but if Forest Berry or another prominent horse pushes Le Grand Etoile along, the resulting honest pace could play into the hands of a closer finishing with momentum; however, Bonjour Belle, Astral Calling, and The Resdev Rocket are redistributed into midfield rather than racing from their true hold-up position, weakening this scenario's credibility substantially. Even if it unfolds, those three may not be far enough back to produce the burst their style requires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If an unexposed runner dramatically outclasses the field in terms of raw ability and wins irrespective of pace shape.
scenarios.body: In a low-grade nursery handicap with compressed ratings from OR 49 to OR 65, the window for a class outlier is narrow, but a horse like Bluestone Lady — a winner over course-consistent going with a healthy sim-going strike rate — could simply have too much ability if she is fitter and sharper than her rivals on the day. This scenario bypasses tactical considerations entirely and is the least dependent on pace dynamics.

watchPoints.text: Le Grand Etoile's uncontested lead — if Andrew Mullen is allowed to bowl along at a completely unchallenged crawl through the first half-mile, the race may be effectively over before the straight begins for the hold-up horses.

Forest Berry's hood and proximity to the pace — Sir Mark Prescott's gelding records in headgear are worth monitoring at the off; if she travels fluently in second, she becomes the most dangerous challenger to Le Grand Etoile and the most likely winner in the dominant scenario.

Bluestone Lady's draw and blinkers — blinkers fitted for the first time or as a retained tool can sharpen a hold-up horse's early positioning; if Paul Mulrennan gets her tracking closer than expected, she upgrades her chance markedly.

The three redistributed hold-up types (Bonjour Belle, Astral Calling, The Resdev Rocket) will likely bunch in midfield — watch for traffic and interference at the two-furlong pole if Le Grand Etoile's pace suddenly quickens and the midfield compresses.

Rule Of The Agency's weight at 134lbs is notable for a horse with limited experience; Jason Hart will need to find a clean run from her natural hold-up position and a pace that truly tests stamina for the full mile.

races.name: 'Celebrating Veteran Armed Forces' Selling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yermanthere
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a strong profile on this exact going — three of last five on Good, winning at 10f on Good and placed twice; Tim Easterby's yard in solid nick (3/90 T14 but volume yard), 37 days fresh and carrying a manageable 140lbs for an 8-year-old who clearly loves this surface and trip.
runners_data.comment: Yermanthere arrives in fine nick, placing second twice in his last two starts and a winner three starts back, with experience over today's trip and going in his favour; the main concern is a trainer operating at just three per cent over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Runninsonofagun
runners_data.note: Front-runner who will go straight to the lead, arriving on just a 7-day turnaround suggesting stable confidence; 9/15 sim-going strike rate and a win at 8f on Good give foundation, but stepping to 1m1f for the first time in recent form is a slight question — his ability to control tempo will define whether he wins or fades.
runners_data.comment: Runninsonofagun caught the eye with a second two starts back and a third four starts back, and at just seven days since his last run he arrives in good order, having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Theme Park
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with an outstanding sim-going record (13/15 on Good) and a sharp recent form line — placed twice and won last time at 8f on Good for Nigel Tinkler; tongue-tie fitted, handles this trip comfortably and Faye McManoman will be able to switch off and stalk the pace before delivering a finish.
runners_data.comment: Theme Park arrives here in excellent heart, placing third last time out and a winner three starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the 138 lb burden is the one factor that could anchor his chances.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Her natural inclination is to come from off the pace, but with so many hold-up horses in this field she will find herself racing further forward than ideal — Alan Brown's runners are 0/6 in the last fortnight, and six runs without a win on the recent form string temper enthusiasm, even with decent sim-going numbers (12/15).
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Princess Niyla does bring distance and going experience to the table, and her third two starts back offers some encouragement, but a seventh last time out is hard to ignore and she faces a stiff task from a field of eleven.

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie sends this 4-year-old out following a 14-day break with Paul Mulrennan aboard; the form string of 765654 is uninspiring and sim-going is mixed (8/13), and though his natural style is hold-up, the crowded rear means he'll race positionally closer than he'd like — his 0W1P strike rate on Good underscores modest claims.
runners_data.comment: Motawaared has been winless in his last six starts, finishing no better than fourth throughout that sequence, and our figures rank him ninth of eleven here, making him hard to fancy at face value; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a 14-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Miners Gamble
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted and racing for Brian Ellison, but sim-going is starkly poor (1/15 on Good) — this horse simply has not shown it on this surface, and the form string includes a 13th on Tapeta and a blank on soft ground; his true hold-up style being displaced into midfield adds a further complication.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Miners Gamble faces a stiff ask here, though he has experience of today's distance and going, and a third last time out offers a crumb of comfort; fresh enough at 17 days since his last run.

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's second string, with a stamina profile that stretches well beyond this trip (placed at 16f and 17f); on Good turf his record is respectable (9/15) and Cam Hardie is a capable handler, but 7f-1m1f recent runs suggest the yard is searching for his optimum — his natural closing style works here if the pace is strong enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Langton Wold faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and returns on a quick turnaround of 12 days, but his recent string of sevenths and eighths makes him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Simple Star
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up performer whose entire recent history is over marathon trips (13f-16f) — coming back to 1m1f is a sharp drop in trip for Gary Rutherford's charge, and while the sim-going mark of 13/15 is excellent, the distance profile is a genuine concern; 0/2 T14 for the trainer.
runners_data.comment: Simple Star brings solid fitness on a 17-day turnaround and has run over today's distance and going before, while a rating of 69 ranks him second among these 11 — the case for him as a leading danger is real; yet he remains winless in his last six starts, which is the nagging concern.

runners_data.name: Titainium
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, tackling 1m1f on Good — a trip and going combination he has limited evidence for (best recent run was 5th at 14f on Good); Oliver Stammers takes the ride for Grant Tuer, whose yard is 1/14 in the last fortnight, and the recent form of 57-876 does not inspire confidence that he can last home if forced to lead throughout.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Titainium at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the concern is a pattern of finishes deep in the field, and 133 lb is no featherweight task from stall four.

runners_data.name: Mayor Of Maghera
runners_data.note: This 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though in a field this packed with closers he is mapped positionally closer than he'd choose; his one recent win came at 9f on Good and he has placed at 8f twice — the step to 1m1f looks a logical progression, but Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim and a blank (0) last time out ask questions.
runners_data.comment: Mayor Of Maghera brings distance and going experience and a win four starts back to recommend him, but he has finished unplaced last time out and has been out of the frame in three of his last four, making it hard to argue he is in the form of his life off 131 lb.

runners_data.name: Falcon Nine
runners_data.note: Extraordinary placings record (2W6P from recent starts, consistently second at 9f-10f on Good) marks Falcon Nine out as a horse who runs honestly every time for Iain Jardine and Oisin Orr; a natural hold-up horse, he will struggle to access his deepest position in this field, but his relentless consistency on Good ground over this sort of trip makes him a constant factor whatever the shape.
runners_data.comment: Falcon Nine has been placed in four of his last six starts, including three consecutive runner-up finishes, yet remains winless in recent starts and his trainer is badly out of form at 4% over the past fortnight — a concern despite him returning on a handy 17-day break with distance and going experience in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Titainium are the two confirmed front-runners in an 11-runner field over 1m1f at Musselburgh on Good ground, and both will be intent on leading from the outset, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a dawdle. Runninsonofagun arrives on a short turnaround (7 days) and has front-running form at this trip, while Titainium steps back up in trip having shown enough gate speed to dispute; between them they should ensure an honest, even gallop that stretches the field out early on this flat track. The field contains considerably more hold-up and prominent horses than can naturally settle at the rear — Mayor Of Maghera, Falcon Nine, Princess Niyla, Motawaared, Miners Gamble and Langton Wold are all genuine come-from-behind types redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the race will be well-strung out in the middle sector and true closers will need a clear run. With two genuine pace-setters driving an honest gallop, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks on Good ground — horses that can travel kindly in midfield before unleashing a sustained late run into the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Strong Finisher
scenarios.trigger: If Runninsonofagun and Titainium push each other along at an honest clip, setting up the race perfectly for a hold-up horse to arrive late.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn energy duelling through the first half of the race, leaving the final climb to those held up and travelling well in midfield; Good ground at Musselburgh rewards horses with a clean, sustained finish rather than a sharp burst.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners (most likely Runninsonofagun) gains a tactical advantage and the pace proves only moderate despite the duel.
scenarios.body: Should the pace settle to something manageable rather than truly strong, the horse on the lead can coast into the straight with a useful reserve and nick it before closers wind up; Runninsonofagun's recent fitness (7-day turnaround, 9/15 sim-going) and Jason Hart's tactical awareness make this a live counter-shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the middle part of the race and the prominent/midfield horses find themselves ideally placed without surrendering their position.
scenarios.body: Mayor Of Maghera, Falcon Nine and Princess Niyla are genuine hold-up horses racing positionally ahead of their natural slot, and if the field bunches they can show their best form from a handy pitch; Falcon Nine's remarkable consistency (six places from six recent runs, 2W6P) makes him the standout in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Crowding
scenarios.trigger: If the sizeable hold-up contingent creates traffic issues and the race is decided by who finds a clear run earliest in the straight.
scenarios.body: With six genuine hold-up types all needing room in the final furlong and true closers having to navigate around each other, a horse with size, stride and a clear passage benefits disproportionately; Langton Wold's stamina profile (placed at 16f and 17f) could prove relevant if the race degenerates into a slog with closers impeding each other.

watchPoints.text: Runninsonofagun and Titainium will go head-to-head for the lead from the off — watch which one (if either) gives way before the bend, as the survivor could steal an uncontested advantage that changes the race entirely.

The large cluster of genuine hold-up horses (Falcon Nine, Mayor Of Maghera, Princess Niyla, Langton Wold, Miners Gamble) all converging into the straight at once creates a significant traffic-jam risk — watch for horses getting blocked and failing to find daylight until too late.

Yermanthere's trainer Tim Easterby has a 3/90 T14 strike rate but Jake Dickson (5lb claim) is riding — the claim brings the weight down and Easterby does place horses carefully at this level; watch if Dickson is instructed to come wide and late off the strong pace.

Theme Park's tongue-tie and Faye McManoman booking is worth noting — Nigel Tinkler often uses McManoman for specific tactical reasons, and a horse with 13/15 sim-going who won last time out at 8f stepping up to 1m1f on identical going is moving in the right direction.

Simple Star's drop from marathon trips (13f-16f) to 1m1f is abrupt — if Gary Rutherford has deliberately targeted this shorter trip as a fitness run or sharpener, the 0/2 T14 figure and the distance change suggest this may not be a maximum-effort start.

races.name: Ina And Ella MacGregor Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Viper
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from Brian Ellison's yard who has finished 1st and 2nd in his last five runs; the presence of Carmel Valley will force a genuine contest for the lead rather than a controlled solo effort, and his last outing was 30 days ago suggesting freshness.
runners_data.comment: Viper won two starts back and was second three starts back, but that ninth last time out clouds his recent profile; he has run over today's trip and returns after 30 days, though carrying 135 lb from stall one will test his stamina.

runners_data.name: The Resdev Scholar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Michael & David Easterby ridden by Joanna Mason returning from 73 days off; nine visits to similar Good going have produced one win and four places, and 7f suits, but the long absence is a notable query on sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Placed in two of his last three starts, The Resdev Scholar arrives here with experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 90 gives him a strong case as a leading danger; the main risk is 73 days off the track without a win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Two Commanders
runners_data.note: Prominent racer stepping up to 7f from a strong run of 6f form for Edward Bethell; three placings from four on Good ground is an excellent strike rate and Oisin Orr is an astute booking, though the step to 7f will need to be handled off what is likely to be a fast early pace.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after back-to-back placed efforts, Two Commanders arrives here 40 days fresh carrying 133 lb from stall five, and while he has run over today's trip, a rating of 79 leaves him mid-pack in a ten-runner field.

runners_data.name: Beyond The Bar
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Tim Easterby who did win over 7f on Good but has run largely at 8f in recent starts and finished down the field there; active at 12 days since last run and Paul Mulrennan rides, but the consistency record here is patchy and the OR of 74 leaves little room for error.
runners_data.comment: Beyond The Bar landed a win three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat off 129 lb from stall 6; the main risk is a cold trainer strike-rate of just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Yy Spirit
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's runner is a true hold-up type with a tendency to fade in the finish; the redistribution to midfield reflects a congested rear rather than a natural positional shift, and with only one similar-going placing from seven attempts, the race shape is unlikely to suit at a price.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Yy Spirit has been out of the placings in three of her last four starts, and her sole recent win came four starts back; a return to form looks needed here, though she does have distance and going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: Carmel Valley
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Katie Scott who has placed twice on Good at 7f and 8f; Cam Hardie rides and will try to share the lead with Viper, but the pair's mutual pressure makes it hard for either to dominate, and her OR of 62 reflects the stiff task ahead.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Carmel Valley faces a stiff ask here, though a third and a second two and three starts back show she can get into the mix, and she has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's hold-up performer placed at 8f on Good but has run five consecutive 4th-or-5th finishes without winning; shown to midfield on the map due to a crowded rear field rather than natural preference, and the unbroken run of near-miss results suggests a talent plateau at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a run of fourths and fifths that makes Light The Night Up hard to fancy from stall seven carrying 116 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and fitness is not a concern after just a 14-day break.

runners_data.name: Blakefell
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's prominent racer won over exactly 7f on Good ground and holds credible form at this course-distance profile; Jason Hart is a strong jockey booking and the trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days, though the horse has mixed his form between prominence and slightly off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Blakefell arrives here in solid nick, second last time out and third two starts back, showing consistent placed form in recent starts, and he has run over today's trip and going before, making conditions familiar ground; the 133 lb ask is the one query.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's prominent runner has won four times from eleven similar-going starts and boasts back-to-back 7f Good-ground wins in recent form; Connor Beasley rides and the record of consistent improvement at this trip marks this horse as one of the key dangers in Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Velvet Rhythm won twice in her last six starts but has an unplaced effort latest, and while she has run over today's trip and going, the 132 lb burden from stall 10 poses a stiff challenge for a filly rated 77 officially.

runners_data.name: Siouxpersonic
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Julie Camacho with a headgear note (h) who is returning from 73 days off alongside The Resdev Scholar; placed twice on similar going but best form came at shorter trips of 5-6f, and the step to 7f after a long absence makes the timing of any late effort uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Siouxpersonic was unplaced last time out, and has a win among her last five starts, with experience over today's trip and going giving her every chance from stall two; the chief concern is a trainer operating at just 4% over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Viper and Carmel Valley are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this 7f Musselburgh trip, creating a genuinely competitive early pace on Good ground rather than the soft, uncontested gallop that would suit either individually. With Two Commanders, Blakefell, and Velvet Rhythm all pushing to race prominently, the pace pressure through the opening two furlongs is likely to be sustained enough to stretch the field and compromise those who burn energy fighting for position. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already congested, but the contested fractions ahead of them are more likely to play into the hands of a patient, well-positioned midfield or prominent horse who can pick up off the pace without getting caught in the early battle. This race shape most favours prominent-to-midfield horses with a proven turn of foot on Good ground — those who can sit just off the contested lead and pounce in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Striker
scenarios.trigger: If Viper and Carmel Valley fight for the lead and set an honest gallop that softens the field for a prominent chaser
scenarios.body: The early contest between the two front-runners burns them both off, leaving the race to a horse travelling smoothly just behind who can quicken on the flat Musselburgh straight; Two Commanders and Velvet Rhythm both have the form and style to exploit this shape, with Velvet Rhythm boasting four wins at 7f on Good in recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner breaks cleanly and the other fails to match strides, leaving a single horse to control an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: Viper, who has won at this distance on Standard going and whose trainer Brian Ellison is in 2/22 recent form, could steal a march if Carmel Valley misses the break or is held back; a controlled, solo lead on Good ground at Musselburgh over 7f is exploitable for a confirmed pace-setter with enough reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves truly strong enough to cause a collapse in the leading group, allowing genuine hold-up types to come through late
scenarios.body: Siouxpersonic or The Resdev Scholar, tracking from midfield-to-rear, could benefit if the fractions are genuinely punishing; The Resdev Scholar has placed form on Good at 7f and Siouxpersonic showed pace at shorter, but this scenario is partly reliant on Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up finding positions they are unlikely to achieve naturally given redistribution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Splits The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and a horse from the middle of the pack threads through a divided field on the flat straight
scenarios.body: Blakefell, who won over this exact 7f trip on Good ground and is ridden by the experienced Jason Hart, has the profile to capitalise on a chaotic mid-race scenario; Beyond The Bar recorded a win over 7f on Good but has shown inconsistency at 8f and would need this specific shape to land a blow at a higher OR.

watchPoints.text: Watch Viper and Carmel Valley at the start — if both jump cleanly and contest the lead stride for stride, the early pace could be significantly faster than this Good ground distance usually demands, dramatically increasing the chance that neither leads home.

Yy Spirit and Light The Night Up are both true hold-up horses pushed forward on the map; if the pace does collapse they may find themselves boxed in rather than finishing through, so monitor their positioning in the first furlong as a marker for whether the field strings out as expected.

The Resdev Scholar and Siouxpersonic are both returning from 73-day absences — if either shows any sign of ring-rustiness in the preliminaries or is notably keen early, discount their closing chance significantly in a race likely to be run at an honest gallop.

Velvet Rhythm's trainer Charlie Johnston has seven runners in the last 14 days from 41 (17% strike rate) and the horse has won four of eleven on similar Going — a live contender whose form profile maps directly onto the most-likely race shape, worth tracking from the two-furlong marker.

races.name: Ocean Scotland Outdoor Advertising Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Opal Storm
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner redistributed to lead as the sole pace-setter; Brian Rothwell's yard is winless in five over the last 14 days but this mare has a recent C&D win in good ground and controls this race from the front — style fit is the concern, as she is naturally a hold-up type pushed forward, so physical exertion of front-running may blunt her finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Opal Storm won three starts back and returns on a sharp 11-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going, with her rating of 58 suggesting she retains ability; the worry is a pair of poor efforts since that victory.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie has five winners from 35 runners in the last fortnight, and this eight-time placed mare on Good going (12 from 15 qualifying runs) is consistent at the level; her hold-up style leaves her reliant on a pace collapse to land a blow, though her habitual place record over 5f at this class suggests she threads into the mix.
runners_data.comment: Wee Mary has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 58 edges above her official mark, suggesting she is capable of going closer than her recent finishes imply; yet to score in her last six starts remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by W H Harrison with limited trainer firepower (0 from 1 in 14 days); her best effort came over 5f Good (placed second) and she handles the trip, though her form string of 649266 suggests she tends to find one or two too good — a hold-up style in a field this congested makes a clear run essential.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a pair of sixths in his most recent outings, Sands Of Seve faces a stiff task ranked ninth of ten on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 25 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: So Grateful
runners_data.note: Easterby yard is in decent nick (3 from 37 in 14 days), and this eight-year-old's recent form of 904222 screams consistent placer — though she is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield mapping slot because of field composition, so her natural late run may be partially compromised; her four sim-going places on Good confirm the surface holds no fears.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in recent starts, So Grateful has been second three times in his last six outings and lines up here with strong claims as one of the top-rated runners in the field; yet to land a win, but the placed form is solid and he arrives fit on 19 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Sixcor
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt sends this veteran out just 14 days after a run and he won over 5f Good in recent form (1 in hist); naturally a hold-up horse placed into a midfield role here because of the crowded rear, and the headgear change to a hood (hg:p) suggests connections are seeking sharper focus early — could be competitive if finding a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Sixcor won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving him some grounding, but a sixth last time out and carrying 127 lb from stall six are checks on confidence, and he sits mid-pack on ratings heading in.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old is absent from winners in 10 runners over 14 days; her 6/9 sim-going record is respectable and a second-place finish over 5f Good is her best effort, but her hold-up style is displaced further forward than ideal due to field shape — the form string of 467926 includes a worrying 9, suggesting inconsistency under pressure.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Gwen Tennyson does at least bring experience of today's trip and going, and her runner-up finish two starts back shows she can threaten; however, sixth last time out and an official mark of 49 suggest she faces a stiff ask from stall eight carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: R Mike Smith's five-year-old (tongue tie, hg:t) arrives 16 days fresh; the form of 775650 is uninspiring and his 12 from 15 Good-going runs reveal he handles conditions without threatening, placed into midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type — he would need the race to fall his way tactically with a gap presenting itself.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Royal Duke does at least bring experience of today's trip and conditions to draw 1 carrying 126 lb, and a speed rating of 58 offers mild encouragement; however, that unplaced effort last time out is hard to overlook for a gelding yet to find his best.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Also trained by R Mike Smith, 14 days since last run and carrying headgear (hg:p); recent form of 623870 includes a zero (non-completion or pulled up) and her placed efforts have come in Soft/Good-to-Soft, making today's straight Good ground worth monitoring — displaced into midfield from her natural hold-up role, and her sim-going record of 9 from 15 is moderate.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, with her most recent efforts yielding only unplaced finishes, Ski Angel is hard to fancy on these figures despite a third and second in recent starts; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and 14 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Lady Bouquet
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's five-year-old returns after 37 days off — the longest layoff in this field — with a hood (hg:p); her sim-going record of 8 from 15 is ordinary and her form of 364349 shows proximity without winning, a genuine hold-up type pushed into midfield because of overcrowding at the rear which further dulls her chances of generating a meaningful late run.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and fourth on two of her last four outings, Lady Bouquet has distance and going experience to call on and our rating of 56 sits well above her official mark; the risk is that she has been winless in recent starts and her last run ended in a disappointing ninth.

runners_data.name: Breeze Star
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's three-year-old has 30 days between runs and a form string of 68-878 that contains a dash (likely a break or rule 4 deduction run) and no placed efforts on Good turf (sim-going 4 from 8, 0W0P); a hold-up type nudged forward on the map who has not demonstrated she can land a blow at this level yet — one to monitor for improvement but the evidence is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sequence of finishes deep in the field, Breeze Star is hard to fancy from a rating of 47 ranked tenth of ten, though he has run over today's distance and going before and 30 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Opal Storm is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this field and will lead from the outset, setting what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good turf over five furlongs at Musselburgh. With no genuine rival willing to press her for the lead, she controls the fractions entirely, meaning the pace is unlikely to be extreme in either direction — a measured, honest clip rather than a true scorcher. The field behind her is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types, with So Grateful, Gwen Tennyson, Sixcor, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Lady Bouquet, and Breeze Star all redistributed forward on the map because there is simply no room for every genuine hold-up runner to find their natural berth in a race this shape — in reality, horses like So Grateful and Sixcor are most likely to secure the best positions just behind the leader, while the deeper hold-up types will be further back than they might prefer. This race shape — a lone leader setting a controlled tempo — favours runners who travel well just off the pace and can deliver a sustained finish rather than a pure late burst, meaning the proximity riders (those with hold-up style but placed just in behind) hold the clearest advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Opal Storm Leads, Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Opal Storm dictates a comfortable solo lead throughout and the field behind fails to reel her in.
scenarios.body: Opal Storm controls pace completely without pressure, conserving energy and kicking clear in the final furlong on her preferred Good turf; her recent course win over C&D gives her concrete grounds for dominance.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Proximity Runners Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled tempo allows the best-placed hold-up types to track up and overhaul Opal Storm inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: So Grateful and Sixcor, both genuine closers finding themselves pushed into midfield on the map, settle closest to the action and produce a sustained rally to catch the leader; Good going suits their recent form patterns and the steady pace means no late collapse in the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Deep Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the race gets unusually strong, allowing true back-markers to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: Wee Mary or Sands Of Seve, producing their characteristic late efforts from off the pace, pick through a tiring field in the final 100 yards; this requires a faster-than-anticipated tempo set by Opal Storm, which is not her natural tendency.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If multiple redistribution horses jostle for position early, creating interference and disrupting the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Traffic problems in the opening stages shuffle the pack and leave the result open to a horse finding a clear run from an unlikely position; Gwen Tennyson or Royal Duke could benefit from a gap if rivals are hampered.

watchPoints.text: Opal Storm is the only genuine pace-setter — if she misses the break or fails to stride on immediately, the entire race loses its shape and the result becomes unpredictable.
So Grateful and Sixcor are both genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield; watch for overcrowding in the early stages as multiple horses converge on the same limited space just behind the leader.
Ski Angel's form includes a zero (likely non-completion) and her best placed efforts have come on softer ground — today's Good turf is worth monitoring on the exchanges as the race unfolds.

Lady Bouquet returns after 37 days, the longest layoff in this field; first-time-back form for Philip Kirby's stable is worth checking, as fitness and ring-rustiness are genuine variables in a sprint handicap.

Breeze Star shows no placed efforts on Good turf across four qualifying runs — in a race where pace control sets a fair gallop, a horse with no closing evidence on this surface is unlikely to land a surprise.

runners_data.comment: Misemerald has shown consistent placing form, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, but she remains yet to win in her last six starts and a rating of 47 suggests she faces a stiff task from stall one carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Thats My Boy Luke is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner mile handicap and, though a natural hold-up type redistributed to the lead by necessity, will likely dictate from the front at a pace he controls rather than one forced upon him — making this a genuinely sustainable, unhurried gallop on Good ground at Musselburgh. The field is saturated with hold-up horses: Due Respect, Approaching Dawn, Joshuas Dream, Misemerald, Caledonian Dream, Abu Royal, Bantz, Sievier and Serengeti Sunrise all want to race from the rear or mid-division, yet with only one horse willing to go forward, many will be shuffled into positions that do not reflect their natural style and cannot all sit where they want. With Thats My Boy Luke able to control fractions unchallenged and a slow-to-moderate tempo likely, horses that can travel prominently or in a handy mid-pack position without cover will be better placed than the true closers. This race shape strongly favours runners who can race handily in the first five or six early on and quicken from a good position, as a compressed field chasing a lone, unhurried leader will leave deep closers with very little pace to aim at late on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Thats My Boy Luke settles into an uncontested lead and dictates a steady pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Dictating every fraction on Good ground around Musselburgh's flat mile, the leader sets a moderate tempo that blunts the closers and rewards anything that can track or press from a handy position; the pack will bunch behind and face a wall of horses when they try to pick up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that midfield horses travelling well sweep past the leader in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop sees the field bunch through the home straight, and runners who have been able to travel smoothly in fourth to seventh off the slow pace find themselves perfectly placed to quicken; horses with strong recent form at this course and distance and good Good-ground records benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Burst Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and creates a vacuum that a back-marker exploits with a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: If the front end ties itself in knots rounding the final bend, a horse with enough class and finish to close from the back quarter of the field could finish fast through a tired pack; however, most true closers here are redistributed types who are unlikely to get far enough back to generate that run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Thats My Boy Luke, racing out of role, fails to find a rhythm and the race deteriorates into a slow-burn sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A stop-start or dawdling pace that produces a chaotic final furlong scramble could see a lightly-weighted horse with a sharp turn of foot steal it, though without a genuine pacesetter this scenario is hard to trigger intentionally and most beneficiaries here lack the finishing speed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Thats My Boy Luke — watch whether he settles into a genuine lead rhythm or idles badly; if he crawls the first three furlongs the entire race shape inverts and any horse able to quicken from mid-division takes over.

Approaching Dawn — Jim Goldie's stable is 5/35 over the T14 window and she is a natural hold-up type mapped forward; if she gets pushed out wide or fails to find a handy position, her form edge is neutralised.

Misemerald — Kevin Stott has strong course form and the horse's consistent placed record makes her a shape beneficiary, but watch whether the hood keeps her settled enough in a big field early; traffic in a bunched finish is a real concern.

Joshuas Dream — trip is a clear unknown having never run beyond 7f; if she fades in the final furlong as the pace profile suggests, she may cause interference in a tightly grouped home straight — worth noting for position when the pace quickens.

Serengeti Sunrise and Bantz — both carry finishing-fade warnings and return from breaks of 105 and 12 days respectively; if either loses action early in the straight, it creates significant traffic risks for closers tracking directly behind them.
